scenes.headline: How SMELT loops a transformer and still pays its FLOPs
scenes.sub: Matching compute, parameters and KV cache at once, on a mixture of experts
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tuba! Looped transformers are usually compared at equal parameters, while quietly spending more compute. SMELT loops and pays the bill. Here's how.

scenes.text: Loop the middle layers, then pay for the extra passes: narrow the width to cut FLOPs, and add experts to buy the parameters back.
scenes.mark: add experts to buy the parameters back
scenes.say: The idea: loop the middle layers, then pay for the extra passes. A narrower width cuts the compute, and more experts buy the parameters back.

steps.say: Take a twelve-layer mixture of experts, and loop its middle six layers twice. Eighteen layers execute, from twelve layers of weights.

steps.note: each looped write is scaled by 1/2
steps.say: Inside the loop, each pass writes to the residual stream at half strength, so repeated visits don't inflate it.
Why only the middle? The first and last layers do specialized work that repetition doesn't improve. And twice beats three or four times.
Left alone, looping six extra layers is a one point five times compute tax. A fair comparison has to hold three budgets at once.
Narrow the hidden width, from twelve eighty to ten fifty-six, and the extra passes fit the same compute per token.
That loses parameters, so widen the expert pool, from a hundred and ninety-two to two hundred and eighty-eight per layer.
Head size and the GQA ratio hold the KV cache level. All three budgets land within four percent.

scenes.label: less training compute to reach the Baseline's loss, on the fitted frontier
scenes.note: scaled to 54B non-embedding parameters; FLOPs, never wall-clock
scenes.say: Matched on all three, looping still wins: six point eight to eighteen percent less training compute for the same loss. Real, but no free lunch.

scenes.text: Looping is a real architectural lever, not just relabeled scale. Just a smaller one, once somebody bothers to check.

recap: Loop the middle half of the layers, twice
Narrow the width, add experts to match
scenes.say: To recap: loop the middle twice, trade width for experts to keep every budget level, and bank a modest, real saving.
